title: Release evidence is bound to criterion receipts at the released SHA, so an unattended release is decided on the same evidence goal closure demands
description:
Filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a from an external review (finding 1), VERIFIED at HEAD fee4e168 and reproduced by probe; correctness refuter FAILED to refute; severity refuter lowered it (human-only path, preview verdict visible in the PR body). OWNER DIRECTION 2026-09-09 REFRAMES THE FIX: "we can approve the plan at the start but that's it" — moe-next must NOT add a preview-approval gate before release. So the reviewer's prescription (require an APPROVED preview via a new RELEASE_PREVIEW_REQUIRED code) is REJECTED. What remains is the reviewer's correct diagnosis: the machine evidence at release is weaker than at goal closure, and that is precisely what must be fixed BEFORE release can be auto-approved. This row is the prerequisite of the auto-approval row.

MECHANISM, measured (reviewer's line anchors did not drift):
- release-durable-facts.ts:34-53 nodeFacts reads each node's GENERAL verifier receipt (`receipt.execution.test`, one command per node) + landing receipt; :52 `sha: receipt.execution.workspaceBinding?.headSha ?? null`.
- release-dossier.ts:84-94 landingOf applies ancestry ONLY to node.landingSha; :109-111 the receipt gap fires only when receipt is null or receipt.sha is null — receipt.sha itself is NEVER ancestry-checked. So the dossier's line "Every cited commit was re-measured as an ancestor of this sha" means the landing commit is in the tree, NOT that any verifier or criterion check ran at the released tree. MEASURED: a dossier whose verifier receipt sha (999…9) is not an ancestor of HEAD (fff…f) yields gaps=0.
- release-dossier-sections.ts:14-21 DossierGapCode roster has 7 codes, none about criterion-at-sha. release-decide-service.ts:151-163 the ONLY evidence gate is releaseDossierGaps.
- grep: no non-test file under apps/daemon/src/release/ imports currentCriterionReceipts / readCriterionEvidence. Only http/document-coverage-criteria.ts and criterion-evidence/criterion-service.ts do.
- CONTRAST, the stronger seam that ALREADY EXISTS: criterion-evidence/criterion-read.ts:29-44 currentCriterionReceipts (latest run COMPLETED, sameCriterionArtifact, receipt PASSED, approved check + criterionDigest match); criterion-artifact.ts:34-61 readIntegratedCriterionArtifact binds every node landing to the integrated sha via merge-base --is-ancestor and checks verifier workspaceBinding.root; goals/goal-close-prerequisite.ts:24-33 GOAL_CLOSE_CRITERIA_UNVERIFIED consumes it. The producer is composed: criterion-runner.ts + criterion-command-edge.ts, wired at daemon-command-registry.ts:417. docs/plans/2026-09-06-repository-delivery-remediation.md:47 says "no composed producer yet" — that line is 3 days stale; the planning architect must re-measure whether the runner is actually TRIGGERED in the normal journey, and if it is not, that is a prerequisite row in dependsOn, never a narrowed DoD.

FIX SHAPE: in readReleaseDossierInput (release-durable-facts.ts:89-114) consume the same criterion-evidence seam goal closure uses, bind per-criterion evidence to the release sha, and extend DossierGapCode with e.g. CRITERION_NOT_VERIFIED_AT_SHA so rowOf (release-dossier.ts:96-122) emits a gap when no PASSED criterion receipt exists at the released artifact. At minimum also route receipt.sha through the ancestry predicate in landingOf/rowOf. Keep the pure core data-only (fixtures + golden in release-dossier.test.ts) and let the durable reader do the store reads, matching the existing split. Do NOT add a preview-required refusal; leave the preview section render-only as the DONE rows task-70a7ccd3 / task-2a345b2e designed it.

Also: gates-compose-journey.test.ts:13-15 claims "ORDERING IS PROVEN BY REFUSAL" but no arm asserts Gate 3 before Gate 2 refuses; under the owner direction that header is simply wrong and should be reworded, not made true. A malformed copy of this row (task-4e7e9f24, empty description) was deleted minutes before this one was filed.
definitionOfDone: A dossier built from nodes whose verifier receipt sha is NOT an ancestor of the release sha lists a gap naming that node (the probe that returned gaps=0 at HEAD now returns a gap), asserted by gap CODE.

A dossier for a goal with an approved criterion that has NO PASSED criterion receipt at the released artifact lists a gap by the new DossierGapCode; a goal whose criteria all carry a PASSED receipt at that artifact lists none. Both arms assert the code, and the new code is added to every roster that enumerates DossierGapCode (grep the SHAPE, not the symbol).

The release reader consumes the SAME criterion-evidence seam goal closure consumes (currentCriterionReceipts / readIntegratedCriterionArtifact), proven by a set-equality arm over the receipts each side reads for one fixture goal — no reimplemented authority in release/.

NO preview-required refusal is added: release-decide-contracts.ts's closed code map stays at its three codes plus any evidence code, and an arm proves release.decide with a REJECTED or absent preview decision is still decided on evidence alone (the owner direction of 2026-09-09). The preview section remains rendered verbatim.

The planning architect records in planningNotes the measurement of whether criterion-runner is actually triggered in the normal journey at HEAD; if it is not, a prerequisite producer row is filed and named in dependsOn before this row's plan is submitted.
gates-compose-journey.test.ts header no longer claims ordering is proven by refusal for the Gate 2 -> Gate 3 edge; the :140-143 arm is kept and its intent documented as the unattended path.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its count line quoted, and pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test EXIT 0 if any dossier section text or gap code the Release card renders changed.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE TWO DEFECTS AND THE PREREQUISITE. NO EDITS.

THIS ROW IS GATED. dependsOn names task-b2b4550835f14b6ebd4a742e1f3b01cf ("Criterion verification runs without a human ADMIN command"), filed while planning this row because DoD 5's measurement came back negative: the criterion runner is composed but NOT triggered in the normal journey. Confirm it reached DONE via get_context.epicSiblings before touching anything. Binding release evidence to criterion receipts while those receipts need two ADMIN commands would make an unattended release IMPOSSIBLE rather than better-evidenced.

DEFECT ONE, read it verbatim at release-dossier.ts:110-112 inside `rowOf`:
`const receiptGaps = receipt === null ? [gapOf("RECEIPT_ABSENT", ...)] : receipt.sha === null ? [gapOf("RECEIPT_SOURCE_UNPROVEN", ...)] : [];`
A present, non-null receipt sha yields ZERO gaps and never reaches `ancestry()`. Compare `landingOf` at :84-93, which DOES call `ancestry(node.landingSha)` and emits LANDING_NOT_ANCESTOR / LANDING_UNMEASURABLE. That asymmetry is the filing's probe: a dossier whose verifier receipt sha is not an ancestor of HEAD returns gaps=0.

DEFECT TWO: nothing under apps/daemon/src/release/ imports `currentCriterionReceipts` or `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact`. Confirm with a grep; the only non-test consumers are http/document-coverage-criteria.ts:27 and criterion-evidence/criterion-service.ts. release-durable-facts.ts reads each node's GENERAL verifier receipt (`receipt.execution.test`, ONE command per node) plus the landing receipt. Per-node is not per-criterion, which is why fixing defect one alone is not enough.

READ THE SEAM YOU WILL CONSUME, so you do not reimplement it: criterion-read.ts:29-44 `currentCriterionReceipts` (latest run COMPLETED, sameCriterionArtifact, receipt PASSED, approved-check and criterionDigest match) and criterion-artifact.ts:34-61 `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact` (binds every node landing to the integrated sha via `merge-base --is-ancestor`, checks verifier `workspaceBinding.root`). goals/goal-close-prerequisite.ts:24-33 consumes it as GOAL_CLOSE_CRITERIA_UNVERIFIED — that is the standard this row is raising release to.

CENSUS THE GAP-CODE ROSTER BY SHAPE, NOT BY SYMBOL. `DossierGapCode` is declared at release-dossier-sections.ts:14-22 with seven codes, and `GAP_SENTENCES` at :45 is a `Readonly<Record<DossierGapCode, string>>`, so typecheck forces a sentence for a new code. A full-tree grep for the code literals and GAP_SENTENCES returns exactly five files, all under apps/daemon: gates-journey-fixtures.ts, release-dossier-sections.ts, release-dossier.ts, release-dossier.test.ts, release-evidence-completeness.test.ts. Confirm that list is still exactly those five.

DEFECT ONE, verbatim at release-dossier.ts:110-112 in `rowOf`:
`const receiptGaps = receipt === null ? [gapOf("RECEIPT_ABSENT", ...)] : receipt.sha === null ? [gapOf("RECEIPT_SOURCE_UNPROVEN", ...)] : [];`

Nothing under apps/control-room. `DossierGapCode` is 7 codes at sections :14-22; `GAP_SENTENCES` at :45 is an exhaustive `Readonly<Record<DossierGapCode,string>>`, so typecheck forces a sentence.

THE SEAM I WILL CONSUME, read and traced to its consumer. `criterion-read.ts:29-44 currentCriterionReceipts(store, goal, artifactRead = readCriterionArtifact)`. WHAT GOAL CLOSURE ACTUALLY CONSUMES, traced end to end: goal-services.ts:166 refuses GOAL_CLOSE_CRITERIA_UNVERIFIED from `goalCloseReadinessFor` -> goal-close-readiness.ts:98 `readGoalCloseReadiness(createDocumentCoverageReadPort(...))` -> document-coverage-read.ts:190 `readCoverageCriterionAuthority` -> document-coverage-criteria.ts:27 `currentCriterionReceipts(store, goal)` with the DEFAULT artifactRead. `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact` is consumed by the criterion PRODUCER (criterion-service.ts:23), NOT by goal closure. 1. `CriterionReceipt` carries `artifact: IntegratedCriterionArtifact` (criterion-contracts.ts:51), so the artifact sha each PASSED check ran at is readable PER CRITERION off the receipt itself. No second store read, so the two-reads-disagree hazard the adversarial pass asks about does not arise.
2. `release-dossier-fixtures.ts:32-35`: `RECEIPT_SHA = sha40("dd")` is NOT in the fixture's `ANCESTORS` set. So step 2's fix reddens the golden and release-evidence-completeness.test.ts until the fixture's receipt sha is made an ancestor. That is adversarial question 4 answered in advance: the fixture WAS quietly wrong, calling itself "evidence complete and re-measurable" while its receipt sha was un-measurable.

CONSEQUENCE FOR gates-journey-fixtures.ts, disclosed now rather than discovered at step 5. `journeyWorld` seeds NO criterion approvals and NO criterion run, so once release consults criterion receipts its Gate 3 "released" arms would refuse RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE. The fixture must seed criterion evidence. The recipe already exists at criterion-read.test.ts:59-72 (approve -> verify queues -> commit RUNNING/COMPLETED run records -> `recordCriterionReceipt` PASSED), and `criterionWorld` is built from the SAME `boundWorld`/`committedRevision`/`approveGate1`/`submit`/`approvePlan` builders `journeyWorld` uses, with the same crit-api/crit-ui ids. `readCriterionArtifact` shells out to git and this lane has no git object database, so `readReleaseDossierInput` needs the artifact read as an injectable seam (the precedent is `criterion-service.ts:18 readIntegrated?`, "Test seam; production always measures the full integrated Git candidate"); the journey then doubles it as its sixth disclosed double, for the same reason it already doubles the ancestry measurement.

PATH SET WILL EXCEED THE PLAN'S 7 keyFiles. Unavoidable and named here: release-dossier-contracts.ts (declares DossierInput, which gains the field) and release-dossier-fixtures.ts (the only other DossierInput producer) are not in the plan's list. Every other DossierInput literal in the repo comes from that one fixture, so no

implementationPlan.description:
ANCESTRY THE RECEIPT SHA (release-dossier.ts) — the smaller half, and it closes the filing's probe.

In `rowOf` at :110-112, a receipt whose sha is present must go through the same `AncestryPredicate` that `landingOf` already applies to the landing sha. A receipt sha that is NOT an ancestor of the released sha is evidence taken from a tree that is not the one being released, and today it reads as clean.

Re-use the existing vocabulary rather than minting more: `landingOf` at :84-93 already distinguishes NOT_ANCESTOR from UNMEASURABLE and formats the detail as `` `${GAP_SENTENCES[code]} (${sha})` ``. Follow that shape exactly so two releases stay diffable, which release-dossier-sections.ts:10-12 says is why rows are sorted in the first place.

KEEP THE CORE PURE. `rowOf` and `landingOf` are data-only; `ancestry` is injected. Do not reach for a store or a git call here — the durable reader supplies the predicate, and the golden in release-dossier.test.ts depends on that split.

Do not change RECEIPT_ABSENT or RECEIPT_SOURCE_UNPROVEN. This step adds a check for a case that currently produces NO gap; it re-classifies nothing that already gaps.
implementationPlan.note:
THE RECEIPT SHA NOW GOES THROUGH THE ANCESTRY PREDICATE. The filing's probe is closed.

PRODUCTION. `rowOf`'s inline ternary at release-dossier.ts:110-112 is replaced by a new `receiptOf(criterion, receipt, ancestry)` that mirrors `landingOf` exactly: null receipt -> RECEIPT_ABSENT, null sha -> RECEIPT_SOURCE_UNPROVEN (both unchanged, nothing already gapping is re-classified), and a PRESENT sha is now passed to `ancestry`. ANCESTOR -> no gap; otherwise a gap whose detail follows landingOf's format `${GAP_SENTENCES[code]} (${sha})`. The core stays data-only: no store, no git, predicate injected.

TWO NEW CODES, NOT ONE, and the module's own doctrine is why. release-dossier-contracts.ts:22-31 states that UNMEASURABLE is never collapsed into NOT_ANCESTOR because "we could not check" and "we checked and it is absent" are different claims; goal-close-prerequisite.ts:38-40 keeps ABSENT and AMBIGUOUS apart for the same stated reason. So RECEIPT_NOT_ANCESTOR and RECEIPT_UNMEASURABLE mirror the LANDING pair rather than sharing one code. DossierGapCode is 7 -> 9 and the exhaustive `Record<DossierGapCode,string>` at GAP_SENTENCES forced both sentences (that guard fired during the edit, as the plan predicted).

THE FIXTURE WAS QUIETLY WRONG, and this is adversarial question 4 answered with a measurement rather than an opinion. release-dossier-fixtures.ts:35 `ANCESTORS` held only the two landings; `RECEIPT_SHA = sha40("dd")` was NOT in it. The fixture's own doc calls its two covered criteria "evidence complete and re-measurable", so the honest repair is to make the receipt sha an ancestor, which I did with the reason written into the fixture. It is not a workaround: it is the fixture finally describing the state it claims.

THREE EXISTING ARMS MOVED, ALL THREE IN THE DIRECTION OF THEIR OWN STATED INTENT ("once per CITED COMMIT, not once per criterion"). There is now a third cited commit.
- "consults the ancestry predicate once per CITED COMMIT": `calls` [ALPHA_LANDING, BRAVO_LANDING] -> [ALPHA_LANDING, RECEIPT_SHA, BRAVO_LANDING]. This list is now ALSO the proof the receipt sha is cited at all — under the old code it could not appear.
- "renders UNKNOWN rather than throwing": consulted 1 -> 2, and the arm now pins the RECEIPT_UNMEASURABLE sentence verbatim with its sha and asserts RECEIPT_NOT_ANCESTOR is absent, so the two receipt codes cannot be swapped without reddening.
- "caches an UNMEASURABLE verdict too": consulted 1 -> 2 for two criteria over one node, i.e. an UNCACHED predicate would now be asked FOUR times. The cache claim got stronger, not weaker.

GREEN, scoped, foreground, count lines quoted:
`npx vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=30000 src/release` -> `Test Files 13 passed (13)` / `Tests 136 passed (136)`, exit 0. Before the arm updates it was `1 failed | 12 passed`, `3 failed | 133 passed`, which is the non-vacuity evidence for this step: the production change moved real assertions.
`... src/gates-compose-journey.test.ts src/http/release-read.test.ts` -> `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 16 passed (16)`, exit 0. The journey survives this half because its substitute predicate answers ANCESTOR for the sha under release and its verifier receipt is bound to LANDED_SHA, which IS that sha.

Scoped runs use `--root . --config package.json` per mem:gotcha-bare-vitest-in-apps-daemon-resolves-the-root-config; a bare `npx vitest` in this package resolves the ROOT config, whose include has no apps/**, and finds zero files. Peer dirt untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
CONSUME THE CRITERION SEAM GOAL CLOSURE CONSUMES (release-durable-facts.ts, release-dossier-sections.ts, release-dossier.ts) — the half that makes the dossier mean what it says.

(1) ADD ONE CODE to `DossierGapCode` at release-dossier-sections.ts:14-22 for "this criterion has no PASSED criterion receipt at the released artifact" — the filing suggests CRITERION_NOT_VERIFIED_AT_SHA. Add its sentence to `GAP_SENTENCES` at :45; the exhaustive `Record<DossierGapCode, string>` will fail typecheck until you do, which is the guard working.

(2) READ THE EVIDENCE IN THE DURABLE READER, `readReleaseDossierInput` at release-durable-facts.ts:89-114. Call `currentCriterionReceipts` and `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact` — the SAME functions goals/goal-close-prerequisite.ts consumes. Do NOT reimplement their rules in release/: `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact` binds node landings to the integrated sha with `merge-base --is-ancestor` and checks the verifier's `workspaceBinding.root`, and a second copy would drift from the one goal closure trusts. That drift is the disagreement this row exists to end.

(3) EMIT THE GAP IN THE PURE CORE. `rowOf` gains the new gap when the criterion has no PASSED receipt at the released artifact. Keep the reader doing store reads and the core doing data, matching the existing split.

(4) The new code must reach every roster step 1 censused. `GAP_SENTENCES` is enforced by typecheck; gates-journey-fixtures.ts and release-evidence-completeness.test.ts are NOT, so check them by hand.

DO NOT TOUCH release-decide-service.ts:151-163. `releaseDossierGaps` is already the only evidence gate, so a new gap code flows to the refusal with no change there — confirm that by reading rather than by editing.
implementationPlan.note:
THE DOSSIER NOW CONSULTS THE CRITERION SEAM. DoD 2 and DoD 3 are delivered here; DoD 3's set-equality arm landed with the production edit because it needed the git-backed lane that already exists in release-durable-facts.test.ts.

(1) ONE NEW CODE. `CRITERION_NOT_VERIFIED_AT_SHA` on `DossierGapCode` (now 10 codes: 7 original + step 2's receipt pair + this) with its sentence "no passed criterion check binds this criterion to a commit this sha contains". The exhaustive `Record<DossierGapCode,string>` refused to compile until the sentence existed.

(2) THE READ, and a MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGED THE PLAN'S INSTRUCTION. Step 3 said call `currentCriterionReceipts` AND `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact`. I call `currentCriterionReceipts` and NOT `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact`, because I traced what goal closure actually consumes and the plan's parenthetical was one function too wide: goal-services.ts:166 -> `goalCloseReadinessFor` -> goal-close-readiness.ts:98 -> document-coverage-read.ts:190 `readCoverageCriterionAuthority` -> document-coverage-criteria.ts:27, which calls `currentCriterionReceipts(store, goal)` with the DEFAULT artifact read. `readIntegratedCriterionArtifact` is consumed by the criterion PRODUCER (criterion-service.ts:23), never by closure. Injecting it here would have made release's receipt set a strict SUBSET of closure's, so DoD 3's set-equality clause — the checkable one, and the one the row is named for — could not have held. Release now reads through the identical call, so the sets are equal by construction of the authority rather than by coincidence, and that is asserted against both production surfaces.

(3) THE GAP, in the pure core. New `criterionOf(criterion, verified, ancestry)`; `rowOf` gains a `verified` map built once in `criterionRows`. No store, no git in the core. Absent receipt -> the bare sentence; present but off-tree -> the sentence plus the artifact sha, matching `landingOf`'s format. The UNCOVERED and SHARED early returns are left alone: those rows already gap, and a second gap on them is noise, not information.

WHY PER-CRITERION AND NOT PER-GOAL, which the plan could not know: `CriterionReceipt` carries its own `artifact: IntegratedCriterionArtifact` (criterion-contracts.ts:51). So each criterion's artifact sha is read off ITS OWN receipt and put through the injected predicate. That answers the adversarial question about reading the store twice for one fact before it is asked — there is no second read to disagree with.

(4) ROSTERS, checked by hand as instructed. gates-journey-fixtures.ts enumerates no code literal (it needed evidence, see below). release-evidence-completeness.test.ts asserts an exact gap list for a receipt-sha-null fixture whose two criteria DO carry criterion receipts, so its expectation is still exactly right and untouched — verified by running it, not by reading it.

release-decide-service.ts IS UNTOUCHED, confirmed by `git diff --name-only` returning zero lines for it. `releaseDossierGaps` at :158 is still the only evidence gate, so the new code reaches RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE with no wiring change.

THREE FIXTURE LANES HAD TO LEARN CRITERION EVIDENCE, and this is the substantive discovery of the step. Before this, NO release fixture had any: every one of them was describing a goal whose criteria had never been checked, which is exactly the state the new gap names.
- NEW SHARED HELPER `seedPassedCriterionReceipts` in criterion-evidence/criterion-test-fixtures.ts. Production writers throughout: `approveCriterionCheck` through the service, the production queue, `recordCriterionReceipt`. Only the run's RUNNING/COMPLETED records are committed directly, the way `criterion-runner.ts`'s module-private `mark` does — the recipe criterion-read.test.ts:59-72 already uses. It reads `contractRef` and `planningRunRef` off the goal's own binding and reads each expectedVersion off the aggregate, so it carries no transcribed value, and it RETURNS the seeded criterion ids so callers assert against what was seeded.
- release-durable-facts.test.ts, THE STRONG LANE: it builds a REAL temp git repository, so the artifact comes from the PRODUCTION `readCriterionArtifact(workspace)` with NO substituted seam, and I assert it equals the released sha before seeding. DoD 3's set equality lives here for that reason: real git, real seam, both sides production, non-empty roster asserted BEFORE the two sides are compared so two equal empty sets cannot pass it.
- http/release-read.test.ts: both criteria seeded, so the surviving difference between its two rows is the NODE evidence the arm actually measures. Seeding only one would have made the covered/UNKNOWN split ambiguous about which authority produced it.
- gates-journey-fixtures.ts: the operator's criterion approvals now sit in the same human sequence as the three gates, PASSED at the sha under release. Sixth disclosed double added to the header, `criterionArtifactAt(sha)`, for the same stated reason as the fifth — this lane

implementationPlan.description:
THE ARMS (DoD 1, 2, 3, 4), each asserting a gap CODE rather than a count.

(a) RECEIPT ANCESTRY, release-dossier.test.ts — a dossier built from nodes whose verifier receipt sha is NOT an ancestor of the release sha lists a gap NAMING that node, asserted by code. This is the filing's probe, which returned gaps=0 at HEAD; it must now return a gap. Add the mirror arm too: an ancestor receipt sha still lists none, so the check cannot be a blanket.

(b) CRITERION AT SHA, release-dossier.test.ts — a goal with an approved criterion that has NO PASSED criterion receipt at the released artifact lists the new code; a goal whose criteria all carry a PASSED receipt at that artifact lists none. Both arms assert the code (DoD 2).

(c) SET EQUALITY, release-durable-facts.test.ts — the release reader and goal closure read THE SAME receipts for one fixture goal, asserted as set equality over the receipts each side reads (DoD 3). Assert against the production surfaces, never against a helper that reimplements them; a helper-backed arm would pass while the two sides drifted, which is the whole failure this row is about.

(d) NO PREVIEW GATE, release-decide-service.test.ts — `release.decide` with a REJECTED preview decision, and again with NO preview decision, is still decided on evidence alone. Assert that release-decide-contracts.ts's closed code map still holds its three codes plus the evidence code, and that the preview section still renders verbatim. This is the OWNER's direction of 2026-09-09 overruling the external reviewer, so the arm exists to stop a well-meaning future edit reversing it.

Every arm names its expected code and, where two layers could answer, which one did (project rail 1).
implementationPlan.note:
NINE NEW ARMS. Every one names its expected CODE, never a count, and every gapping arm has a mirror so it cannot be a blanket.

(a) RECEIPT ANCESTRY, release-dossier.test.ts, new describe "release dossier binds evidence to the released tree".
- "gaps a verifier receipt taken on a tree the released sha does not contain": the filing's probe. `RECEIPT_NOT_ANCESTOR` on crit-alpha, asserted as an exact {code, criterionId} list. It ALSO asserts through `criterionRows` that the row NAMES the node (nodeKey node-alpha) and still shows the sha it cited, and that the gap detail contains that sha — DoD 1 says "naming that node", and DossierGap carries only a criterionId, so the naming lives on the row. MIRROR in the same arm: an ancestor receipt sha lists NOTHING.
- "keeps a receipt git could not decide apart from one git decided against": UNMEASURABLE and NOT_ANCESTOR asserted as DIFFERENT codes in one arm, so collapsing the pair reddens. This is the arm that guards the doctrine at release-dossier-contracts.ts:22-31.

(b) CRITERION AT SHA, same describe, four arms.
- "gaps an approved criterion with no passed criterion check, and lists none when it has one" — all three cases in one place: no receipt at all -> the code; a receipt for a DIFFERENT criterion -> still the code (so a goal-level "some receipt exists" check cannot pass it); all criteria carrying a passed check -> empty. That is DoD 2's two directions plus the mis-attribution case.
- "gaps a criterion check that passed on a tree the released sha does not contain" — NOT_ANCESTOR and UNMEASURABLE artifacts. PASSED alone is not enough; the artifact goes through the same predicate the landing does.
- "decides PER CRITERION: one verified criterion does not cover the goal's others" — two criteria, one seeded. A per-goal check reports both clean or both gapped, so this arm is what makes the per-criterion design checkable.
- "says in the document that the criterion was not verified, rather than dropping the row" — the rendered markdown carries the sentence AND no longer carries "Every cited commit was re-measured as an ancestor of this sha", which is the false line the filing objected to.

comments.author: worker-b42eccd4
comments.content:
EVIDENCE 2 of 2 — THE ADVERSARIAL PASS, question by question, plus two disclosed residuals.

Q1. CAN A DOSSIER REPORT ZERO GAPS WHILE A CRITERION HAS NO EVIDENCE AT THE RELEASED TREE — WHAT PATH? I found three candidate paths and closed two by reading production.
(a) A goal with ZERO criteria renders no rows, so gapsSection prints its all-clear sentence. But release-production-wiring.ts:59 refuses first: `if (input === null || input.criteria.length === 0) return null`, and a null facts read is RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE at release-decide-service.ts:154. Not reachable through release.decide.
(b) UNCOVERED and SHARED criteria return early from `rowOf` and therefore carry NO criterion gap. They already gap (CRITERION_UNCOVERED / RECEIPT_SHARED_NODE), so the row is never clean. Deliberate: a second gap on an already-gapped row is noise, and I chose not to double-report.
(c) RESIDUAL, DISCLOSED: the artifact is bound by ANCESTRY, not equality. A check that passed at an ancestor of the released sha reports clean, so commits landed AFTER the check are not themselves criterion-checked. I kept ancestry on purpose — it is the same standard the landing commit and the verifier receipt are held to, and `currentCriterionReceipts` independently requires the run's artifact to equal the CURRENT workspace artifact by root AND sha AND treeSha, so in the normal journey the artifact IS the workspace head. Tightening to equality is a one-line change in `criterionOf` if the board wants it; I did not take it unilaterally because it would refuse a release of a descendant commit that the landing checks already accept.

Q2. DOES THE NEW GAP FIRE FOR A GOAL WITH NO APPROVED CRITERIA, AND IS THAT RIGHT? It does not fire, because there are no rows to fire on — and that is neither a false alarm nor a hole, because such a goal cannot reach the gate at all (Q1a). A gap needs a criterion to name; the right refusal for "no criteria" is the one that already exists.

Q3. TWO READS OF THE SAME FACT THAT COULD DISAGREE MID-RELEASE? No, and the design choice is what removes the question: `CriterionReceipt` carries its own `artifact` (criterion-contracts.ts:51), so each criterion's artifact sha is read off ITS OWN receipt in the same pass that read the receipt. There is no second store read of the artifact to drift from the first. The pure core then consults the memoized ancestry predicate once per distinct commit.

Q4. DID THE RECEIPT-ANCESTRY CHECK CHANGE AN EXISTING FIXTURE, AND WAS THAT FIXTURE QUIETLY WRONG? Yes, and yes. release-dossier-fixtures.ts:35 `ANCESTORS` held only the two landings; `RECEIPT_SHA` was absent, while the fixture's own doc called its two covered criteria "evidence complete and re-measurable". It read that way only because nothing measured it. Repaired by adding RECEIPT_SHA (and the new CRITERION_ARTIFACT) with the reason written into the fixture.

Q5. IS RELEASE NOW AT LEAST AS STRONG AS GOAL CLOSURE? Clause on each side:
- CLOSURE: goal-services.ts:166 refuses GOAL_CLOSE_CRITERIA_UNVERIFIED unless readiness is READY or NO_CONTRACT; readiness comes from the coverage read whose verified set is the KEYS of `currentCriterionReceipts(store, goal)` (document-coverage-criteria.ts:27, default artifact read).
- RELEASE: release-decide-service.ts:158 refuses RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE on ANY gap; `criterionOf` gaps unless the criterion is in `currentCriterionReceipts(store, goal)` — the identical call with the identical default — AND its artifact is an ancestor of the released sha.
So release is closure's condition PLUS an at-sha binding closure does not perform, PLUS the landing and verifier-receipt ancestry it already had. Strictly stronger, in two places, and equal in the one that matters (the receipt set). It is also stricter on the NO_CONTRACT branch: closure lets a goal with no approved contract through, release refuses it.

CHECKLIST RESIDUALS.
- CONCURRENCY: the whole path is read-only. `criterionReceiptsOf` catches and answers [], which is fail-CLOSED (empty means every criterion gaps). Two concurrent releases are still fenced by the existing admission-journal replay check.
- NEW COST ON A READ PATH, DISCLOSED: `readCriterionArtifact` spawns four git commands, and the release CARD read now reaches it. It is bounded — `currentCriterionReceipts` short-circuits on `latest?.status !== "COMPLETED"` before calling it, so a goal with no completed criterion run spawns nothing, and a goal with one spawns it once per read. The card already shells out to git for ancestry.
- INHERITED CONSTRAINT, WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: `readCriterionArtifact` returns null on a DIRTY worktree. Release therefore now requires a clean tree to see criterion evidence — exactly as goal closure already does, through the same function. That is the row's intent rather than a regression, but on this shared always-dirty checkout it means the live daemon will refuse a release until the tree is clean.
- PER-FILE CAP: release-dossier.ts is 263 lines, over the 250 target and well under the 400 split threshold; sections 156, contracts 204, durable-facts 147, release-evidence-read 254. gates-journey-fixtures.ts is 414 and its own header states a fixture module carries no line cap.
